# SCSE3040 --- Lab Practicals

**Machine Learning Operations · B.Tech CSE 5th Semester · Bennett University
· Session 2026-27**

Thirteen practicals, one per fortnight, all building the same running project:
a **food delivery-time predictor**. Each one picks up exactly where the last
one stopped, so the arc across the semester is

> notebook -> package -> tracked experiments -> API -> container -> cluster
> -> logs -> automated pipeline -> monitoring

*This file is generated by `scripts/build_labs.py`. Edit the practicals in
`scripts/labdefs/`, not here.*

## What you need

| | |
|---|---|
| Machine | Any laptop with **8 GB of RAM**. Nothing here needs a GPU. |
| Disk | About 3 GB free, most of it for Docker in P08. |
| Software | The course virtual environment --- see [SETUP.md](SETUP.md). |
| Internet | Only for the one-time setup, and for P08's first image build. |

Only **P08** needs anything beyond the course environment: Docker Desktop.
P09 runs real `kubectl` commands if a cluster happens to be available, but
every graded task in it works without one.

## How a practical works

Every notebook has the same three parts, in this order.

1. **Walkthrough.** Numbered steps you read and run. It works as shipped, so
   your teacher can project it and demonstrate. Nothing here can be got wrong.
2. **Your turn.** Three tasks. Each has a stub with `# TODO` in it and a hint.
   Do them in order; they get harder.
3. **Self-check.** One cell that marks your work and prints a `PASS`/`FAIL`
   table. Run it as often as you like --- it never breaks your notebook, and a
   task you have not started simply shows `FAIL`.

## Running a practical

```
cd labs\P01-workbench
..\..\.venv\Scripts\python -m jupyter lab P01.ipynb
```

Then work down the notebook, pressing **Shift + Enter** in each cell. Always
run the cells in order from the top.

If everything goes wrong: **Kernel -> Restart Kernel and Clear All Outputs**,
then start again from the first cell. Nothing is damaged by doing this.
